VALUE CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: sheet's Capacity=37213.00 scm/yr is indeed implausibly small, and the source explains why. OPEC ASB2013 Table 4.10 lists this exact row ('Bouri (offshore)/Bahr Asslam (Sabratah platform)', 4in) with a raw Capacity figure of '37,213' — but the table's own column header states the Capacity units are '(1,000 scm/yr)' (confirmed by re-reading the printed header above the Libya-cont'd block; the same header governs the whole continued table). So the source's true value is ~37,213,000 scm/yr (≈37.2 million scm/yr / ~0.037 bcm/yr), not 37,213 scm/yr — GEM appears to have dropped the '×1,000' multiplier when transcribing, understating capacity by three orders of magnitude. Recommend Update correct Capacity to 37213000 (scm/yr) or equivalent ~37.213 mmscm/yr. The ref itself (this Wayback ASB2013 snapshot) is valid and does contain the digits '37,213' exactly as entered — flagging the units/scale error for Update, not withholding the ref.

OPEC ASB2013 Table 4.10: 'Bouri (offshore)/Bahr Asslam (Sabratah platform)' = 12.4 miles (=19.96 km) — closely matches sheet's 12.00 mi (19.31 km), simple rounding. Cross-checked ASB2017 Table 9.9 ('Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016'): 'Bouri offshore/Bahr Es Salam (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas | 2 x 12 [mi] | 4, 10 [in]' — confirms ~12 miles recurs across editions, paired with the 10in line (=P1859). Second, structurally-independent source: Mellitah Oil & Gas's own 2019 prequalification tender (PRQ/JPT/005/19, 'Bouri Gas Upgrading Project') specifies '10" CS and 4" CS pipelines 20 km long connecting DP4 to Sabratah Platform' for dehydrated gas/condensate export — same diameter pairing (10in/4in) and closely matching length (20km≈12.4mi) for the same field-pair. Caveat: this 2019 document describes BGUP's NEW/planned pipes (feasibility stage in 2019; Saipem's ~$1bn construction contract came in 2023; first gas still being targeted for Sept 2026 per Libya Herald), not necessarily the same physical asset the 2011-2013-vintage OPEC ASB entries describe — so not treating this as a fully independent corroboration of the SAME pipe, but its matching specs for the same corridor add credible context. Verifier flags both PDFs 'missing expected substring' (cannot parse embedded PDF text); both manually confirmed via pdftotext.

OPEC ASB2013 Table 4.10 lists this row under the 'Libya' country section (Owner/operator 'Mellitah Oil and Gas'), and Bouri and Bahr Essalam/Sabratah are both offshore fields in Libyan waters (Bouri ~120 km NW of Tripoli per Mellitah's own 2019 document; Bahr Essalam/Sabratah similarly offshore NW Libya) — start/end Libya/Libya is uncontested across every source consulted.

NOT a duplicate — sources indicate GEM's P6709 and P1859 represent two genuinely different, parallel physical pipelines on the same Bouri-to-Bahr Essalam/Sabratah corridor, not a double-count of one line. Evidence: OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin tabulates this field-pair as TWO adjacent-but-separate rows in every edition checked (ASB2012, ASB2013, ASB2017): a 10-inch line carrying dehydrated GAS and a 4-inch line carrying CONDENSATE. ASB2017 Table 9.9 makes the pairing explicit: 'Bouri offshore/Bahr Es Salam (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas | 2 x 12 [mi] | 4, 10 [in]' — the '(2)' notation plus '2 x 12' means two parallel 12-mile lines, one 4in and one 10in. Independently, Mellitah Oil & Gas's own 2019 prequalification tender for the 'Bouri Gas Upgrading Project' (BGUP) describes new '10" CS and 4" CS pipelines 20 km long connecting DP4 to Sabratah Platform for dehydrated gas and condensate export' — the same twin-diameter, same-route configuration (gas line + separate condensate line). So P6709 (4in) = the condensate line, P1859 (10in) = the gas line of the same corridor: different specs because they are different pipes, not a GEM data error in that specific sense. Two open caveats worth flagging to the researcher, though: (1) P1859's GEM length (32 km) doesn't match the ~12-12.4 mi (~19-20 km) that ASB2013/ASB2017 converge on for BOTH lines — 32km (=20mi) traces to the earlier ASB2012 edition's figure for that same row, which later ASB editions revised down; P1859's length may merit a separate correction check. (2) The mellitahog.ly 2019 document frames its 10in/4in pipes as NEW/planned BGUP construction (feasibility stage 2019; Saipem's ~$1bn contract 2023; first gas still targeted Sept 2026 per Libya Herald), while the OPEC ASB entries (2011-2013 data) already show a same-diameter pairing years earlier — implying an older, smaller Bouri-Sabratha tie-in predates BGUP and BGUP is now building new/expanded twin lines of the same diameters on the same route. Current-day operating status of GEM's specific P6709/P1859 assets vs. the incoming BGUP lines is not resolved by the sources found; recommend a follow-up check once BGUP reaches first gas (targeted Sept 2026) to confirm whether these rows should be updated to as-built BGUP specs or retired/merged.
